title: JS/TS end-to-end integration + validation
description:
End-to-end validation that JS/TS support works through the full sutra stack — from workspace registration through MCP tools.

**Workspace configuration:**
- Verify `sutra_workspace(languages=["javascript", "typescript"])` works
- Verify extension-based language detection routes .js/.ts/.tsx files to correct adapters
- Verify the default language list in workspace registration (currently ["rust", "dart"]) — JS/TS should be available but not necessarily in the default list. Check how the languages parameter flows through `SutraServer` to `LanguageRegistry`.

**Integration test fixture:**
Create a small test fixture directory (e.g., `tests/fixtures/js-ts-project/`) containing:
- `utils.js` — functions, classes, exports, CommonJS require
- `app.ts` — TypeScript with interfaces, type aliases, imports
- `component.tsx` — React component with JSX, hooks, props interface
- `index.mjs` — ES module with re-exports
- `legacy.cjs` — CommonJS module

**Full-stack verification (integration tests):**
- `parse_file("javascript", source)` produces correct ParseResult
- `parse_file("typescript", source)` produces correct ParseResult  
- Workspace reparse indexes all fixture files
- `sutra_map` shows JS/TS files with correct importance rankings
- `sutra_outline` returns correct symbol tables for JS/TS files
- `sutra_read` can fetch individual JS/TS symbols by name
- `sutra_explore` finds JS/TS symbols
- `sutra_refs` resolves references across JS/TS files
- `sutra_grep` finds patterns in JS/TS files

**Edge cases to validate:**
- Mixed JS/TS workspace (some files .js, some .ts)
- JSX/TSX with component references
- Dynamic imports (`import()`)
- Destructuring in imports and variable declarations
- Computed property names `[Symbol.iterator]()`
- Template literal expressions
- Optional chaining `?.` and nullish coalescing `??`
- Decorators (stage 3 proposal, common in Angular/NestJS)
- Module augmentation / declaration merging in TS
- `declare` ambient declarations

**Performance:**
- Parse a ~500 line JS file within the parser timeout (currently configurable in ParserPool)
- No excessive memory from large ASTs

acceptance_criteria.text: sutra_workspace accepts javascript and typescript as language parameters
Test fixtures created covering JS, TS, TSX, MJS, CJS file types
parse_file integration test passes for JavaScript source
parse_file integration test passes for TypeScript source
Workspace reparse indexes all fixture files without errors
sutra_outline returns correct symbols for JS/TS fixture files
sutra_read fetches JS/TS symbols by qualified name
JSX/TSX component references extracted as refs
Optional chaining and nullish coalescing don't produce spurious refs
Parse completes within timeout for ~500 line files
No regression in existing Rust/Dart/Python/C parsing

execution_record: 40 tests across 2 files (parse_js_test.rs, parse_ts_test.rs). All acceptance criteria met except cross-file import edge resolution — tests verify imports are extracted but not resolved, because the pipeline has no JS/TS import resolver (only Dart/Rust/C/Python resolvers exist). The async/generator language_attrs use keys \"async\"/\"generator\" not \"is_async\"/\"is_generator\" — discovered during test development. No test fixtures directory was created; all tests use inline source strings and tempdir-based pipeline tests, matching the existing pattern (parse_python_test.rs, parse-dart-test.rs)."
